fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Why He Sees a Decedent Estate at Birth", "body": "Kallenbach argues that when the cord is clamped and cut, the rest of the baby, the umbilical and extra-embryonic material, stays behind, and that the birth certificate is issued to those human remains, giving rise to a decedent estate held in trust. He reads the back cover of Right-of-Way, a cut cord beside a chalk outline, as a crime scene. In his telling, that severed material loses its self-government and can be plugged into a 1789 constitution or the Vatican, while his own constitution is mind, body and spirit, the government upon his shoulders from Isaiah 9:6. He also casts public policy as an insurance policy."}, {"title": "Kallenbach on Fertilization and Innocence", "body": "Kallenbach's simplest formula is that fertilization equals innocence, while the birthday equals guilty or not guilty, which he calls the original sin that lower courts build on. He treats a life as one continuous, contiguous story from a single-cell zygote to last breath, citing Luke 5:31, they that are whole need not a physician. He says the zygote holds both intelligent design and evolution, against the either-or framing he dates to the 1925 Scopes trial, and reads I and my father are one as the zygote, which he says shares his 46 chromosomes, like the oak and the acorn. He calls the birthday the greatest implant of all time."}, {"title": "Right-of-Way, Mayhem and His Letter to HHS", "body": "The book's title, Kallenbach explains, comes from the cord as the only way out of mother: cut it and, in his view, we are landlocked and have literally lost our way. Reading Black's Law Fifth Edition, he ties the right-of-way rule to precedence and to enlarge, which also means to set at liberty one held in custody. Chance notes that the 1828 dictionary sends mayhem straight to maim. Kallenbach then reads his letter to HHS Secretary Becerra, which frames the cut as medical mayhem, cites the medical definition of delivery as a fetus and its membranes, and recasts COVID as a covered infant ID."}, {"title": "Reading Old Dictionaries for Hidden Stories", "body": "Kallenbach says he arrived at all of this by chasing every possible definition of a word until the definitions tell one story, and he argues that Black's Law Dictionary tells a story of decedent estates. He explains the period after the R in his own name as separating the living man from the fiction, and cites a 1773 preface to the Memoirs of the Medical Society of London on fellows and corresponding members. The co-host adds the many definitions of order and the Norman and Saxon split between swine and pork, while Kallenbach points to Edwin Abbott's 1884 Flatland and to placenta meaning flat cake."}, {"title": "The Placenta's Spiritual Role, as They See It", "body": "Chance lays out a view he often shares, that the placenta may act like a spiritual guardian angel or psychopomp, and adds that wisdom without acting on wisdom is not really wisdom, so reclaiming the whole story from fertilization can come down to a choice and a symbolic action. The co-host suggests keeping any such reset private, as simple as a shower or a change of clothes. Kallenbach keeps to biology and definitions instead: he reads Madonna and child as placenta imagery the Church of Rome depends on, argues that humans never ate the placenta, and ties the manger, a feed trough, to the afterbirth."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if your birth certificate was issued to the human remains left behind at birth, not to you? Kurtis R. Kallenbach, author of Right-of-Way, decodes the placenta mystery, the birth certificate as decedent estate, and the legal fiction obscuring your true biological identity.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: This conversation covers the birth certificate as legal fiction and decedent estate, fertilization as the origin of innocence and self-governance, the umbilical cord as your legal right-of-way, Kallenbach's letter to HHS Secretary Becerra identifying the COVID narrative as "covered infant ID," the placenta as guardian angel and spiritual body, mayhem as the legal felony of cord-cutting, the birthday as the greatest belief implant ever installed, and how reclaiming the full story of your biology from fertilization to last breath restores self-governing authority over your entire estate.
